title: No yes-or-no questions
statement: Never ask a question a student can answer yes or no or by a two-way pick: ask what or how, and give choice questions several plausible options.
example: A blocking checklist row requires 4 or more plausible options on every choice question and zero two-option coin flips.
detail: A content review of a reading lesson asked that a yes-or-no question be dropped altogether, even though the app said it couldn't be answered yes or no, and recast as a what question (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-aladdin-2026-08-25/feedback-text.txt`). The course's QC checklist makes it a blocking row: every choice question has 4 or more plausible options and there are no two-option coin flips (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`, row B8).
against: A later run found: A Grade 9 unit's knowledge base ends each lesson's closing questions on an 'X or Y?' evaluation and flags a question that is not 'X or Y' as merely descriptive, and its lesson design specification's evaluation example asks learners to pick one of two readings and justify the view (`g9/sources/1. Act 1 - Knowledge Base - Overview.csv`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/codex-history-extract/CODEX-HISTORY-EVERYTHING-OUT.md`).
